description: Comprehensive coverage of secure software development, OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities, exploit mitigation techniques, security testing, and integrating security into the SDLC. Students complete CTF challenges and build secure applications from scratch.
key_topics: Secure coding practices and defensive programming|Web application vulnerabilities (XSS, CSRF, SQLi, SSRF)|Authentication & authorization systems|Cryptographic implementation and API security|Security testing and static/dynamic analysis

description: Prepares cybersecurity professionals to understand, apply, evaluate, and defend artificial intelligence in security contexts. Structured as Learn → Use → Evaluate → Defend: students build accurate mental models of machine learning and large language models, apply AI to core defensive workflows, rigorously validate AI outputs against ground truth, and study how AI systems are attacked and defended. Hands-on work runs on locally hosted models, with student-built fine-tuned models evaluated on NYU's Torch supercomputer.
key_topics: ML, LLM, and reasoning-model foundations for security practitioners|Prompt engineering for log analysis, alert triage, and threat intelligence|AI-assisted secure code review and software supply chain security|Evaluating AI outputs (precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC)|Prompt injection, data poisoning, and adversarial ML (OWASP LLM Top 10, MITRE ATLAS)|Defending AI systems, AI governance, and the NIST AI RMF

description: Policy frameworks for responsible AI deployment, operational safety in AI systems, regulatory policy development, adversarial robustness, and designing decision-support tools aligned with human values.
